# `third_party/harfbuzz`

TeX Live 2026's own HarfBuzz, **unmodified**, for the Unicode mode's shaping
(`docs/design/xetex/PLAN.md` §3.1, phase S1). XeTeX shapes every native-font
word with HarfBuzz (`XeTeXLayoutInterface.cpp`'s `layoutChars`), so its output
depends on HarfBuzz's exact version; FlashTeX uses the one TeX Live 2026's
`xetex` is built with. Built by `crates/flashtex-xetex/fontlibs`
(`flashtex-xetex-fontlibs`).

## Pin

| | |
|---|---|
| Upstream | TeX Live source tree, GitHub mirror <https://github.com/TeX-Live/texlive-source> |
| Tag | `tags/texlive-2026.1` ("texlive-2026.1 tag based on r78399") |
| Commit | `6a300188053b8f2ded89dbd52293732a706b9c0e` (the same pin as `third_party/pdftex`, `third_party/zlib`, `third_party/xetex`) |
| Path | `libs/harfbuzz/harfbuzz-src/` |
| Version | 12.3.2 (`libs/harfbuzz/version.ac`; TeX Live imported <https://github.com/harfbuzz/harfbuzz/releases/tag/12.3.2/> on 2026-01-25, `libs/harfbuzz/TLpatches/ChangeLog`) |
| Fetched | 2026-10-04 |

`crates/flashtex-xetex/tests/pinned_libs.rs` fails if the linked library's
`hb_version_string()` is not the version above, if this table says another,
or if any file differs from `SHA256SUMS`.

TeX Live's changes to the upstream release (`libs/harfbuzz/TLpatches/TL-Changes`)
are removals only: `src/hb-version.h` (regenerated by `configure` from
`src/hb-version.h.in`), `src/hb-features.h.in`, dot files and the `.ci`,
`.github`, `docs`, `perf`, `subprojects`, `test` and `util` directories. No
source file is patched.

## Files

`version.ac` is TeX Live's `libs/harfbuzz/version.ac`, unmodified: the build takes HarfBuzz's version from it, as TeX Live's configure does (`hb-version.h` is generated from `src/hb-version.h.in`).

`harfbuzz-src/` holds 361 files (5.2 MB): everything TeX Live's `libharfbuzz.a`
compiles (`libharfbuzz_a_SOURCES` in `libs/harfbuzz/Makefile.am`:
`src/harfbuzz.cc`, `src/graph/gsubgpos-context.cc` and the 16
`src/hb-subset*.cc`) with every file they include under TeX Live's
configuration (the compiler's own dependency list, `-MM`), the public headers
TeX Live installs (`libs/harfbuzz/include/Makefile.am`, including
`hb-graphite2.h` for S2), `src/hb-version.h.in`, and `COPYING`, `AUTHORS`,
`README.md`. Checksums of every file are in `SHA256SUMS`:

```sh
cd third_party/harfbuzz && shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS
```

Left out of TeX Live's 509-file tree: `src/rust/` and `src/wasm/` (the
HarfRust/fontations and WebAssembly-shaper parts), `src/ms-use/`, the unit
tests (`src/test*.cc`), the Python and Ragel generators (`*.py`, `*.rl`; their
generated `*-table.hh`/`*-machine.hh` are vendored), the meson/CMake build
files, the docs and images, and the headers and sources of backends TeX Live
does not build (Cairo, GObject, GLib, ICU, FreeType's `hb-ft.h`, Core Text,
DirectWrite, GDI, Uniscribe, HarfRust, kbts). `src/harfbuzz.cc` itself
`#include`s the `.cc` files of several of those backends
(`hb-coretext*.cc`, `hb-directwrite*.cc`, `hb-gdi.cc`, `hb-glib.cc`,
`hb-ft.cc`, `hb-graphite2.cc`, `hb-uniscribe.cc`, `hb-wasm-api.cc`,
`hb-wasm-shape.cc`), each wrapped in its own `#ifdef HAVE_...`; they are
vendored, unmodified, so that the amalgamation compiles as written, and
compile to nothing here.

## Build

`crates/flashtex-xetex/fontlibs/build.rs` compiles `src/harfbuzz.cc` with the
`cc` crate as C++, with TeX Live's flags:

| Flag | Source | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `-DHAVE_CONFIG_H` | automake `DEFS` | `hb.hh` includes `config.h` |
| (`-DHB_NO_MT`) | `AM_CPPFLAGS`, `libs/harfbuzz/Makefile.am` | **left out here**: TeX Live builds HarfBuzz without locking (XeTeX is single-threaded); FlashTeX's engine may move between threads (`Globals` is `Send`), so HarfBuzz keeps its mutexes and atomic lazy globals. Locking changes no shaping result |
| `-DHAVE_FALLBACK=1` | `AM_CPPFLAGS` | builds the `fallback` shaper (`hb-fallback-shape.cc`), last in the shaper list |
| `-I<config dir> -I harfbuzz-src/src` | `DEFAULT_INCLUDES`, `AM_CPPFLAGS` | `config.h`, `hb-version.h`, sources |
| `-O2` | autoconf's default `CXXFLAGS` | applied whatever the cargo profile |
| `-fno-rtti -fno-exceptions` | `configure.ac` (GCC/clang) | as upstream intends: no C++ runtime type information or exceptions |
| `-fvisibility=hidden -fvisibility-inlines-hidden` | `KPSE_COMPILER_VISIBILITY` | symbol visibility only; static linking is unaffected |
| (no `-std`) | `AX_CXX_COMPILE_STDCXX([11])` | configure reports "supports C++11 features by default... yes", so it adds none; nor does this build |

`config.h` is `crates/flashtex-xetex/fontlibs/config/harfbuzz/config.h`: the
file TeX Live's `libs/harfbuzz/configure` writes (run unmodified on macOS on
2026-10-04), except that `HAVE_GRAPHITE2` is left undefined and its header and
function checks are made per target (`__has_include`; the POSIX functions off
Windows). Its defines: `HAVE_OT`, `HAVE_CXX11`, `ALIGNOF_STRUCT_CHAR__=1`,
`HAVE_ATEXIT`, `HAVE_ROUND`, the C header checks (`HAVE_STDBOOL_H`,
`HAVE_STDINT_H`, `HAVE_INTTYPES_H`, ...), `HAVE_UNISTD_H`, `HAVE_SYS_MMAN_H`,
`HAVE_XLOCALE_H` (macOS), `HAVE_MMAP`, `HAVE_MPROTECT`, `HAVE_SYSCONF`,
`HAVE_GETPAGESIZE`, `HAVE_ISATTY`, `HAVE_NEWLOCALE`, `HAVE_STRTOD_L`,
`HAVE_POSIX_MEMALIGN`, the `PACKAGE_*` strings, and `AC_USE_SYSTEM_EXTENSIONS`'
`_GNU_SOURCE`/`_DARWIN_C_SOURCE` group. They select platform facilities
(memory-mapped blobs, locale-independent `strtod`, aligned allocation), not
shaping behaviour. `HAVE_FREETYPE`, `HAVE_ICU`, `HAVE_GLIB` and the other
backends are undefined, as in TeX Live: XeTeX builds its `hb_face_t` from
FreeType tables itself (`XeTeXFontInst.cpp`, `hb_face_create_for_tables`), and
HarfBuzz's Unicode functions are its own UCD tables (XeTeX's ICU Unicode
functions are compiled only `#if !HB_VERSION_ATLEAST(2,5,0)`).

`hb-version.h` is generated from `src/hb-version.h.in`, substituting
`@HB_VERSION_MAJOR@`, `@HB_VERSION_MINOR@`, `@HB_VERSION_MICRO@` and
`@HB_VERSION@` with 12, 3, 2 and 12.3.2, which is what TeX Live's
`config.status` writes (checked byte for byte on 2026-10-04).

The subsetter sources (`hb-subset*.cc`, `graph/gsubgpos-context.cc`) are
vendored, so the tree is TeX Live's whole `libharfbuzz.a` source set, and not
compiled: XeTeX never calls `hb_subset_*`, so a static link of TeX Live's
archive leaves their objects out of `xetex` too (they are unreferenced).

**Graphite2 (phase S2).** TeX Live builds HarfBuzz with Graphite2
(`HAVE_GRAPHITE2`, `KPSE_GRAPHITE2_FLAGS`). S2 vendors TeX Live's Graphite2 and
defines `HAVE_GRAPHITE2`, which compiles `hb-graphite2.cc` and adds the
`graphite2` shaper. Without it, OpenType shaping is unchanged: XeTeX passes
the shaper list explicitly (`XeTeXLayoutInterface.cpp`, `layoutChars`): `"ot"`
alone when the font name asks for no renderer (the comment there: "Since 'ot'
shaper never fails, we set the shaper list to just include it") or for
`/OT`, and `"graphite2"` only for `/GR` (`XeTeX_ext.c`, `loadOTfont`); the
fallback to HarfBuzz's default list is taken only when the requested shapers
all fail, which `"ot"` never does. So only `/GR` fonts (and the Graphite
feature queries of `XeTeX_ext.c`, which go through
`hb_graphite2_face_get_gr_face`) need S2.

## Licence

HarfBuzz is under the "Old MIT" licence (`harfbuzz-src/COPYING`), which is
GPL-compatible and permits use in MIT code. Checked on 2026-10-04, file by
file (a scan of every vendored file for its notice, plus a search for
`Apache`, `GPL-3`, `LGPL`, `MPL` and `SPDX-License-Identifier`):

- 276 files carry HarfBuzz's Old MIT notice; 85 carry none (the `src/OT/`
  table code, the generated tables such as `hb-ucd-table.hh` and
  `hb-ot-tag-table.hh`, `harfbuzz.cc`, `AUTHORS`, `README.md`) and are covered
  by `COPYING`, which covers the package unless a subdirectory has its own
  `COPYING` (only `src/ms-use/` does; it is not vendored).
- `src/hb-algs.hh` also contains a function under the MIT (Expat) licence
  (Zilong Tan's fasthash), whose notice is in the file.
- **No Apache-2.0 code**: the only match for "Apache" is the language name
  in `hb-ot-tag-table.hh` ("Jicarilla Apache"). No GPL-3, LGPL or MPL text.
  `src/rust/` and `src/wasm/` are not vendored.

Belief, not checked: the generated Unicode tables (`hb-ucd-table.hh`,
`hb-unicode-emoji-table.hh`, `hb-ot-shaper-use-table.hh`) derive from
Unicode Character Database files, whose Unicode licence is permissive and
GPL-compatible; the legal review of DESIGN.md §3 covers it.
